newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kinshasa asks Liechtenstein to freeze Mobutu funds.
newsitem.headline: Kinshasa asks Liechtenstein to freeze Mobutu funds.

text.p: Rebels who seized power in former Zaire, renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo, have formally asked Liechtenstein to freeze deposed dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's assets, their representative in Geneva said on Thursday.

Jose Mutombo-Kady told Reuters Zairean prosecutors sent the request last week to Liechtenstein for a total freeze on any bank accounts the cancer-stricken former ruler may have in the tiny principality.

Switzerland has already responded positively to a similar request this month and frozen assets including a sprawling, 30-room villa valued at more than $5.5 million, one of a string of luxury homes he owns around the world.
But Swiss federal police spokesman Falco Galli said his government still lacked detailed information from Kinshasa on Mobutu's assets in the Alpine country.
"We asked Congo's authorities to give us more information. This request will be sent to Congo's justice ministry next week. We need details on Mobutu's funds in Switzerland," he said.
The unprecedented Swiss freeze on May 17 came hours after Mobutu fled into exile before rebels took over Kinshasa and their leader Laurent Kabila proclaimed himself head of state.

Swiss media reports claim Mobutu, reputedly one of the world's richest men, may have had a $4 billion fortune looted from his mineral-rich African country stashed away in numbered secret bank accounts here.
But Mutombo-Kady said the new rulers in Kinshasa estimated Mobutu's wealth abroad at $15 billion and claimed much of it was in Switzerland.
